title: Cold-start GET can create duplicate singleton configuration rows

evidence.quote: This is a singleton table - only one row exists

reasoning: GET /whisper/models calls get_or_create_config even though the endpoint is otherwise a read operation. get_or_create_config performs a non-atomic select-then-insert and ClientConfig uses a random UUID primary key, so two concurrent first requests against an empty database can both observe no row and commit separate singleton rows. Later reads use select(...).first() without an ordering or uniqueness guarantee, so active_model can come from an arbitrary row after the race.
reproduction: Start with an empty client_config table and issue two concurrent GET /config/whisper/models requests using separate sessions. Both can enter get_or_create_config before either commit completes, resulting in two client_config rows.
recommendation: Enforce the singleton invariant at the database or key level and make get_or_create_config retry-safe. For example, use a fixed singleton primary key or unique singleton column, catch the duplicate insert/IntegrityError path, roll back, and re-read the existing row deterministically.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for GET /whisper/models, and the repository search only found frontend mock data plus transcription/service tests, not concurrent cold-start coverage for this route or get_or_create_config.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend test that invokes GET /config/whisper/models concurrently against an empty test database with independent sessions, then asserts exactly one client_config row exists and both responses return the same active_model.
minimumFixScope: Update get_or_create_config and the ClientConfig singleton enforcement; include an Alembic migration only if the fix adds or changes a database constraint/column.
